content:
SECTION 1

* Young people in the UK, especially those in their 20s, are finding it very hard to afford to buy a home because house prices are high and banks are less willing to give out loans.
* A 24-year-old named Sam Webb is frustrated that older generations criticize young people for spending money on things like holidays or meals out, instead of saving every penny for a house deposit.
* Sam feels that many young people may never be able to own a home and will be stuck renting forever, giving their money to landlords who then criticize them for being irresponsible.
* Young people under 25 are legally allowed to be paid less than older workers, even when doing the exact same job, with some earning as little as £5.60 per hour if they are between 18 and 20 years old.
* Because of these lower wages and the likelihood of being on uncertain zero-hours contracts, young people simply do not earn enough money to save up for a house, making homeownership even more out of reach.
